As a result, the E7X is a joint venture between Audi and SAIC, with Audi’s traditional four-ring logo dropped in favour of capitalised AUDI lettering instead. 

The question is, what else has changed? Let’s take a closer look… 

Starting with the design, although the size is relatively similar to an Audi Q8, there is almost nothing else that distinguishes it as an Audi. Whereas all German manufacturers' cars will follow some of the same design cues, if you were to remove the AUDI badging from the front and rear, you’d be hard-pressed to know what the brand was! Still, up front it looks modern and futuristic, with thin headlights and a wraparound loop design that features Matrix LED lights. Along the side, the similarity to the Q8 is more noticeable, although the surfaces of the panels are smooth (similar to an iX3), and around the back the design is relatively clean and similar in look & feel to the front end. 

Step inside, and it’s a similar story to the exterior - the design is totally different to what you would find in a German-built Audi. The main feature you’ll notice is a long screen that stretches across the entire dash, with a passenger screen also built into it. The infotainment system is relatively fast and easy to use, but thankfully, the climate controls are adjusted separately with physical buttons! Elsewhere, the cabin is covered in soft-touch materials, including an Alcantara-effect roof lining, and the seats are incredibly comfortable. 

For those in the back, there’s also a huge amount of space, with reclinable seats, leg rests, and a 27-inch retractable screen! There are also large, sturdy tables built into the back of each of the front seats.

The Audi E7X comes with two motors that combine to produce 680hp and 800Nm. So it’s no slouch, but then again, being electric, it tips the scales at a hefty 2,600kg. It comes with a 100kWh battery, which is good for a claimed range of around 400 miles.

The E7X is on sale in China at an incredibly low price, starting from just £36,360! That’s less than half the price of a similar-sized Audi Q8 from Germany. The question is, if this car were on sale in the UK, would you choose it over a Q8? Let us know in the comments!

videos.summary_source_text:
DRAMATIC Finish | 2026 Danish Golf Championship Relive the final round drama in the Back 9 on Sunday, presented by Nexo, as Jeff Winther secured victory at his home Open.

This win marks Jeff Winther’s second DP World Tour title in four years, making him only the second Danish player to win the Danish Golf Championship, following Rasmus Højgaard in 2023.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

The DP World Tour returns to action after a three-week break with the penultimate event of the Closing Swing at the Danish Golf Championship. Great Northern will host its first DP World Tour event this week, following in the footsteps of Himmerland, Silkeborg Ry Golf Club, Lübker Golf Resort and Furesø Golf Klub in staging this event. The course is the passion project of Thomas Kirk Kristiansen, a fourth-generation member of the family behind the Lego Group. This event has long been renowned for its bumper crowds and the home fans will have plenty of local talent to cheer for this week. 2023 winner Rasmus Højgaard and fellow Ryder Cupper Thorbjørn Olesen are in action, as is rising star and reigning Australian Open champion Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen. Jacob Skov Olesen is looking to continue his rise, while DP World Tour winners Jeff Winther, Niklas Nørgaard and Lucas Bjerregaard are also in action.

Welcome to the Official YouTube channel of the DP World Tour. Every week you can find extended tournament highlights and individual player highlights from the likes of Rory McIlroy, Justin Rose and Tommy Fleetwood. videos.title: Bedard Disguises Every Shot. You Don't.
videos.summary_source_text:
Bedard Disguises Every Shot. You Don't. Watch any Connor Bedard highlight reel and pay attention to the goalie instead of the puck, because what you’ll notice is that the goalie isn’t beaten by speed, he’s beaten by timing. He starts his reaction after the puck has already left the blade, and that gap is the whole story of the Bedard release.

Most players load their shot in a way that tells the goalie everything. The stick comes back, they push down, the blade opens, and by the time the puck actually leaves, the goalie has been reading the shot for half a second and is already square to the shot. Bedard only the other hand changes the angle noticably, where he pulls the puck in tight underneath his body, stacks his weight right over top of it, and lets the shot come off low on the blade in one motion so there’s no dusting it off or telegraphing to react to. Then right at the end he changes the angle, so even a goalie who guessed the timing right is now set for a shot that’s coming from somewhere else.

The part that matters for your game is that none of this is a talent you’re born with. It’s a sequence of mechanics, the puck position, deception, the contact point on the blade, and each one can be trained on its own before you put them back together at full speed. Players spend years shooting a thousand pucks a day trying to shoot harder when the faster path is usually learning to hide the shot they already have.

videos.title: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast Explained: 750 Tokens/Sec, But There’s a Catch
videos.summary_source_text:
GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast Explained: 750 Tokens/Sec, But There’s a Catch https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services
OpenAI says GPT-5.6 Sol can run up to 14X faster with its new Ultrafast mode, reaching as much as 750 output tokens per second. But once you look at the benchmarks, hardware, pricing, and what “Ultrafast” actually means, the story gets much more complicated.

In this video, I break down GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast, OpenAI’s partnership with Cerebras, the 750 tokens/sec speed claim, and the evidence behind that headline 14X number.

More importantly, we clear up one of the biggest points of confusion around the launch: GPT-5.6 Sol, Ultra, Fast, and Ultrafast are not the same thing. Sol is the model, Ultra uses multiple agents in parallel, Fast is a priority processing tier, and Ultrafast uses Cerebras hardware to dramatically accelerate token generation.

We’ll also look at the numbers behind the hype. Cerebras measured a 5.6X end-to-end speedup in its own comparison, while OpenAI’s advertised 14X figure remains a best-case “up to” claim without a publicly disclosed testing methodology.

Then there’s the part that could matter even more: cost. Ultra can use multiple agents—and potentially far more tokens—while Ultrafast still has no publicly listed price.

So is GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast actually a breakthrough? Is 750 tokens per second useful in the real world? And is OpenAI really delivering a 14X speed improvement?

Here’s what the numbers actually tell us.

videos.title: You Hate Your Saggy Chest (HERE'S HOW TO FIX IT!)
videos.summary_source_text:
You Hate Your Saggy Chest (HERE'S HOW TO FIX IT!) Build a Muscular Chest Here - https://athleanx.com
Subscribe to This Channel Here - https://bit.ly/2b0coMW

If your chest won’t grow no matter how much you bench press, this video explains the REAL reason your pecs may not be responding and what you can do to finally build a bigger chest. I’m breaking down chest growth, pec activation, bench press technique, chest genetics, dips, pushups, cable presses, fly variations and the mistakes that can keep your shoulders doing the work instead of your chest.

A lot of guys assume a lagging chest simply needs more weight, more exercises or more volume. But if you’ve been consistently bench pressing for a long time and your pecs still aren’t growing, the problem may not be effort. It may be that your chest is never becoming the dominant muscle in the exercises you’re using.

The bench press should absolutely be a foundational chest exercise. If you haven’t been bench pressing consistently for at least a year, you may simply need more time building strength and improving your technique.

For many lifters, the anterior delts and triceps dominate pressing movements. You may be moving impressive weight without creating enough tension in the pecs. That’s why chest adduction exercises can be so important.

Exercises that bring the arm across the body can help you learn how to contract the pecs more effectively and carry that chest activation into your pressing exercises.

Cable crossovers and cable flys are great options. If you don’t have a cable machine, a dumbbell floor fly can be a useful alternative. I prefer the floor fly to a traditional dumbbell bench fly because the floor limits the bottom range and can reduce the vulnerable position of the shoulder.

But activation is only part of the story.

At some point, chest genetics and skeletal structure matter too. The width and length of your clavicles and your overall frame influence how much total muscle mass your chest can visually carry. That doesn’t mean you should blame genetics. Different lifters simply have different ceilings and chest shapes.

The goal is to maximize YOUR pec development by building the lower chest line, improving thickness through the middle pecs and developing the upper chest so you create that fuller shelf near the clavicles. 

You do this by training the chest with intent instead of treating every chest exercise like a strength test.

One major change is to separate strength training from hypertrophy focused chest training.

Let the barbell bench press be a strength exercise if that’s where you perform best. Then use other chest exercises with lighter weights, slower reps and more control to make the pecs do the work.

On a dumbbell bench press, try pausing at the bottom of each rep. Keep the shoulders back and think about initiating the press with the chest instead of simply driving the dumbbells upward. That brief pause can help eliminate momentum and force you to create tension with the muscle you’re trying to grow.

The same idea applies to dips.

Dips can be an excellent lower chest exercise, but only if you perform them correctly. If your shoulders roll forward as you press up, you may be shifting stress away from the pecs while putting the shoulders in a less favorable position. Slow the movement down, maintain control and initiate the rep with the chest.

Another excellent option is the cable bench press. This doesn’t replace the regular bench press. Instead, the cables pull slightly outward, forcing the pecs to contribute more strongly through their adduction function. For someone who struggles to feel their chest, this can be a game changer.

And if you train at home with no equipment, you can still improve chest activation with pushups.

Slow the pushup down. Don’t just think about pushing your body away from the floor. Think about lifting your sternum as you press and squeezing the pecs to move your torso upward. That can make a pushup feel completely different.

If your chest won’t grow, don’t automatically assume you need more weight, more sets or more exercises. 

First make sure your pecs are contributing the way they should. Improve your mind-muscle connection, control the eccentric, slow down your reps, use exercises that reinforce horizontal adduction and stop letting the shoulders dominate every press.

If you’re looking to build a bigger chest, increase pec activation, improve your bench press technique, grow your upper chest, build your lower chest or finally fix a stubborn chest that refuses to grow, these principles will give you a much better path forward.

videos.title: Förståelsen bakom den magiska cirkeln…
videos.channel: Bättre & Enklare golf med Marcus Edblad PGA
videos.summary_source_text:
Förståelsen bakom den magiska cirkeln… Att svinga under axlarna till över axlarna skapar omgående en effektiv och avslappnad rörelse med maximal hastighet och bra riktning. 

Vi behöver rotera för att hjälpa våra händer förflytta sig men allt annan rotation är bortkastad energi.

#golf #golftips #golfswing 

0:00 Intro till från under till över

Nu finns det möjlighet att genom appen Skillest göra mig till din personliga tränare. Du hittar mig på denna länk: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

Låt mig hjälpa dig finna bättre slag, bollträff, riktning och svinghastighet. Oavsett om du slår en wedge, järnklubba eller driver kan du med dina händer lära dig golfslag som du inte trodde var möjliga. Längre och rakare slag kräver alltid träning men något alla kan lära sig.  

Vare sig du kämpar med en slice eller en hook så har jag videos som kan guida till bättre golf. Är du nybörjare så kan du börja med min grönt kort eller nybörjarkurs.

Försök ersätta dåliga vanor med nya bättre vanor. Oavsett vilket loft eller skaft din klubba har så är det du som bestämmer vad som ska hända. Oavsett om det står callaway, ping, titleist eller taylor made på klubban så kan du slå bra slag.

Var noga med vad du tittar på. Det finns många duktiga instruktörer på nätet, några av mina favoriter är Mike Malaska, Mike Dunaway, Mike Austin.

Försök fokusera på grunderna i slaget bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår. Träna med fördel på en sak i taget. Tränar du din svinghastighet måste du tillåta att det går snett och tränar du raka slag kan du inte samtidigt svinga i max fart.

Ha tålamod och låt det ta sin tid, luras inte av genvägar som bara gör att du tappar fokus från det viktiga. Golf kommer alltid vara svårt men vi kan med träning se till att vi blir bättre för varje dag som går.

Titta mycket på golf på TV. Bryson Dechambeu, Dustin Johnson, Rory Mcilroy kan inspirera till längre slag och andra som Tiger Woods, Viktor Hovland, Ludvig Åberg och Phil Mickelson kan ge dig fantasi att skapa nya slag.

Träna styrketräning för hela kroppen för att må bra genom livet och skapa en effektiv maskin. Träna händer, handleder och armar för att skapa en effektiv release och mer svinghastighet.

Du kan finna inspiration i filmer som Happy Gilmore, Tin Cup eller Bagger Vance. Filmer som Rocky kan ge dig motivation att ta dig till gymet. Legender som Arnold Schwarzenegger, Sylvester Stallone eller Hulk Hogan kan få dig att vilja bli starkare och Moe Norman, Arnold Palmer, Ben Hogan, Sam Snead eller Jack Nicklaus kan inspirera dig att bli en bättre golfare. 

Ge aldrig upp i sökandet och träningen för att få bästa bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår.

Filmat med iPhone 17 och redigerat i iMovie på en Macbook. Att svinga under axlarna till över axlarna skapar omgående en effektiv och avslappnad rörelse med maximal hastighet och bra riktning. 

Vi behöver rotera för att hjälpa våra händer förflytta sig men allt annan rotation är bortkastad energi.

#golf #golftips #golfswing

videos.title: The understanding behind the circle of speed…
videos.channel: Better & Easier golf with your guide Marcus Edblad
videos.summary_source_text:
The understanding behind the circle of speed… From under to over the line of the shoulders will give you a powerful and effective swing with the club. The circle of speed is born.

#golfswing #golf #golftips 

Online lesson are now a possibility on Skillest: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

0:00 Intro to how to feel an effortless golf swing. 

Let me help you get an effortless golfswing with speed, distance and accuracy. I call it the circle of speed. A good release will help you to a better impact and longer drives and irons without slice and hook. How to swing a golf club need to be adjusted to your skill level and experience. 

Long and straight is the goal for everyone but it takes time. Try to focus on one thing not everything when you practise. Impact, face control and swingpath will always be the most important part to drill. We focus too much on rotation but no good golf shot will be executed just by rotating. 

We also need to understand that many myths in golf are misleading. Everything that you find on the internet isn’t true. Ben Hogan, Sam Snead are two of the legends that are often misunderstood.  To understand golf we need to take it step by step and learn every part of the swing before we move on to the next. It's like a big jigsaw puzzle that we all can figure out. 

A will never call a slice sexy but a high draw is beautiful in a very special way. Some pro's that hit draw: Rory McIroy, Xander Schauffele, Patrick Reed, Sepp Straka, Bryson Dechambeau  and many, many more. 

We shall not keep our head still, only start with the hips, look only at the ball or keep the left or right arm straight. Understand what do do with the club and let your body find the best way possible. 

This is not Rick Shiels, Saguto golf, Danny Maude, Meandmygolf, the Average Golfer, Malaska, Mark Crossfield, Alex Elliot Golf or Paige Spiranac. This is a method that anyone can learn if you give it a chance. 

If you use callaway, ping, titleist, takomo or taylor made clubs doesn’t matter you can learn to hit good golf shots. Your loft or your shaft on the club will not change but you can always get better. 

Find what inspires you. Golf basics are the same for everyone. The pga tour, longdrivers or other good golfers can all help you find better golf shots. Watch what they do instead of listed to what they say. Listen mostly to your body and figure out what you need to do to produce the same results as the pros on TV. Be careful when you watch a golf swing in slow motion. The result isn't always what the golfer is trying to do. Feel and real are seldom the same. 

We can find inspiration in a lot of things. You can find training motivation watching movies like Rocky, Tin Cup or Happy Gilmore and find mental inspiration in legends like Arnold Schwarzenegger, Hulk Hogan, Sylvester Stallone or Mike Tyson. Maybe we sometimes need to hear about crazy achievements from people like David Goggins, Jocko Willink, Ct Fletcher, Jim Rohn or Tony Robbins. 

Mike Malaska, Mike Austin, Mike Dunaway, Pete Cowen and Steve Pratt are some of my favorite golf instructors online. Find the tips that make your golf better. Decide what you want to hit. I teach a draw but many like a fade and nobody likes a hook or slice. 

Your hips or your lag is not the key to golf. Your hands will decide the shot and you can do like Tiger Woods and trust your hands. Teach your hands to hit different shots. Hit big hooks and slices to understand what happens. Only straight is not gonna teach you anything. 

Bryson Dechambeu and Kyle Birkshire can inspire you to hit it longer. Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson can give you inspiration and motivation to test new things and new golf shots. Linn Grant, Viktor Hovland and Ludvig Aberg can show you the future of golf. 

The Masters, Players Championship, The Players, The Open and US Open can make you love golf even more. See the best in the world solve all the problems we all need to master any golf course. Golf is a craft and you need fantasy, feel and skills to master it.

Questions my videos will answer:

How to swing faster. How to hit longer. How to swing faster. How to hit your irons better. How to be better at anything. How to master the circle of speed. How to get a better short game. How to hit your wedge better. How to release the golf club. How to rotate in golf. Best tips for beginner golfers. How to hit down on the ball. How to hit up on the ball. How to rotate hips in the golf swing. How to hit straight every time. How to stop slicing. How to swing effortlessly.

The Real Warning Sign of B1 Deficiency (Not Fatigue) The most dangerous sign of a vitamin B1 deficiency involves the heart. If you're low in B1, you might experience fatigue and tingling in the hands or feet, but a severe deficiency may lead to wet beriberi. This condition affects the heart’s ability to pump blood properly.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/3RKMEeP

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements. 

Signs can include:
• Shortness of breath
• Swelling in the legs
• A racing heart
• Fluid buildup in the lungs

Refined carbohydrates, heavy alcohol use, bariatric surgery, and prolonged diuretic use can all increase the risk of vitamin B1 deficiency. If you notice these symptoms, get checked by your doctor and make sure you’re getting enough vitamin B1. Opt for the natural form, allithiamine.

The Real Reason You Keep Getting Leg Cramps at Night Are leg cramps waking you up at night? Discover what causes leg cramps at night, how to stop nighttime leg cramps, and what you can do to get better sleep.

0:00 Night leg cramps
0:40 The causes of leg cramps at night

2:19 Magnesium for leg cramps not working
3:13 What causes magnesium deficiency?
4:43 How to stop leg cramps 
5:40 Magnesium glycinate  
6:28 Severe leg cramps 

👉 Download Dr. Berg's Free Daily Health Routine: https://drbrg.co/45tKUKl

Keep watching for more on magnesium:
▶️ https://youtu.be/2qu59nPJXcg
▶️ https://youtu.be/1gGI_98xzgE
▶️ https://youtu.be/7lSQ2hnycLg

Learn more about how to choose the right magnesium supplement here: https://drbrg.co/4zim0ep

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements. 

Nighttime leg cramps are not caused by a problem with the muscle itself. They’re related to the nervous system. 

Leg cramps at night are typically a direct result of a magnesium deficiency. Some people think magnesium isn’t improving their leg cramps, but they may simply be taking the wrong form. Magnesium glycinate is one of the best-absorbed forms of magnesium.

Magnesium may not stop your leg cramps if you’re also low in vitamin D. Magnesium and vitamin D work together, so the more magnesium you take, the more vitamin D you need, and vice versa.

If you have severe leg cramps, it may take longer to see results.
